prTitle: feat(uptime-assertion-in-checks): Adding assertion_failure_data to the eap_converter
stackAndServices: Python/Django monolith (sentry) consuming a Kafka topic (`uptime-results`) via an Arroyo consumer (src/sentry/uptime/consumers/results_consumer.py); results are converted into wide-column EAP/Snuba trace-items (ClickHouse-backed analytics store, src/sentry/uptime/consumers/eap_converter.py + search/eap/uptime_results/attributes.py) and re-exposed via a DRF endpoint (project_uptime_alert_checks_index.py + serializers.py) read by a React/TypeScript frontend (static/app). The actual HTTP probing AND assertion evaluation is performed by a completely separate service, github.com/getsentry/uptime-checker (Rust), declared as a containerized devservices dependency of this repo and reached only via Kafka — i.e. the feature's core causal step lives outside the diff's own repository.
compiledPromise: FEATURE SPEC: Uptime Monitoring custom assertions — a user attaches an assertion tree (status-code / JSON-path / AND/OR/NOT) to an uptime monitor via the assertion builder UI (shipped in an earlier sibling PR); the external uptime-checker probes the real target URL on schedule and evaluates the assertion against the live response. PR #106833 is the ingestion-pipeline segment that takes the checker's raw `assertion_failure_data` (present in the Kafka CheckResult only when the assertion FAILED) and threads it: Kafka result -> EAP trace-item attribute (JSON string) -> registered EAP attribute -> `/checks/` API field `assertionFailureData`. DISCRIMINATING CLAIM: for a check run against the monitor's real, currently-configured assertion, when the live response genuinely violates the assertion, the specific failure detail (which node of the tree failed) is durably persisted on that exact check's own record and is retrievable by a user, in a fresh session, through the front door (Alerts > Uptime Monitor > Checks, or the resulting Issue) — not just present in the raw API payload. NEGATIVE (must also hold): when a later real check on the same monitor PASSES, that check's own record shows no assertion-failure detail at all — no leakage/staleness of the prior failing check's data onto the passing one (a real risk here because eap_converter.py only sets the `assertion_failure_data` key when it is not None, i.e. it omits the key entirely on success rather than writing an explicit null, which is exactly the shape of bug a sparse/wide-column store can hide).
conjureFeasibility: Partially real, cleanly boundable. The Kafka/EAP/API leg (everything this diff touches) is fully real under CONJURE: `uptime-results` is a first-class devservice topic and EAP/Snuba is standard repo topology. The HARD part — genuine assertion evaluation against a real HTTP response — is NOT in this repo at all; it lives in github.com/getsentry/uptime-checker (Rust), which devservices/config.yml declares as a `remote`, `containerized` dependency (branch: main). CONJURE-by-topology is honestly able to pull and run that container against a harness-controlled test endpoint (e.g. a local HTTP server the harness flips between passing/failing bodies), so this is NOT a doubled/stubbed leg in principle — but it is a cross-repo, cross-language conjure step the harness must explicitly discover and pin (verify uptime-checker's pulled SHA actually implements assertion evaluation, not just that a container starts). The user-facing rendering leg is SEALED OUT entirely: at this PR's merge commit (2026-01-28), no frontend code renders `assertionFailureData` anywhere (the dedicated tree UI landed 5 days later in PR #107065; issue-evidence wiring landed the next day in #107268) — so no amount of conjuring makes a front-door visual confirmation possible for the exact code fingerprint under review. That forces CND regardless of environment quality.
verdictBasis: From the diff + system alone: this PR only adds plumbing (Kafka result -> EAP attribute -> API field); it changes zero frontend code. I confirmed via merge timestamps across the sibling PR chain (105842 builder UI Jan13, 106626 config model Jan23, 106895 endpoint/grouptype Jan28 15:45, 106833 this PR Jan28 20:30, 107268 issue-evidence Jan29, 107065 frontend tree-view Feb2) that at the moment this diff became 'the exact code built+run,' no rendering surface existed anywhere in the product for `assertionFailureData` — a user restricted to click/type/navigate/read (P' clause a) has no DOM element, badge, or drawer that shows this data; only a raw network-response inspection would reveal it, which is disallowed as request-forging-adjacent, not a user-shaped read. Confession: the underlying plumbing plausibly works — the code path is straightforward JSON round-tripping — but 'plausibly works' is exactly the claim P' forbids substituting for an observed, front-door, fresh-session confirmation. NOT-EXECUTED (no reachable front door) maps directly to mechanism 1.3 -> CND. Not covered: I could not determine, from the diff alone, whether the sparse-attribute-omission risk I flagged (success checks never writing an explicit `assertion_failure_data: null`, only omitting the key) actually causes stale-value leakage inside EAP's storage/query layer — that requires runtime behavior of Snuba/ClickHouse I did not execute.
holds: Write-set-bound oracle (1.1) maps cleanly onto this feature: the effect is a genuine per-check EAP trace-item write, FK-causally tied to a specific check_id/span_id, so a harness diffing the store around a single test-check's window would correctly isolate the new attribute to that one row rather than mislocating the oracle.

Calibrated mutation-attribution (1.2, idle-baseline) is directly exercised by real code here: results_consumer.py's create_backfill_misses periodically writes synthetic 'missed window' check rows (now also stamping assertion_failure_data=None) completely independent of any user action. A naive diff-the-whole-store approach during a user's test-check window could misattribute one of these background backfill writes as a false confirmation of the user's action; FK-causal binding to the specific check the user actually triggered correctly excludes it.

The theory's insistence on dual-leg (persisted + fresh-session front-door) confirmation is exactly what keeps an agent from manufacturing a false WORKS here: the API response genuinely does contain the new field and it would be very tempting to declare WORKS on that basis alone, but P'(a)'s front-door-only constraint correctly blocks that shortcut and forces the honest CND.

CONJURE-by-topology correctly surfaces (rather than hides) the fact that the feature's real causal step lives in a separate repo/service (uptime-checker) — the devservices manifest makes this discoverable and, in principle, real-conjurable rather than requiring a stub, which is the theory working as intended for a legitimately complex, multi-repo system.

breaks.detail: P'(a) (front-door only) and the CORE PRINCIPLE's 'bind verdict to the exact code fingerprint' combine to force CND on essentially every backend/ingestion-only PR in a codebase that habitually ships frontend and backend in separate PRs — which, empirically, is Sentry's dominant delivery pattern (I sampled ~15 large-looking PRs across three feature areas — uptime assertions, user feedback AI titles, feature-flag suspect heuristics — and found almost none mixed FE+BE in one diff). The theory cannot currently distinguish 'this backend slice is correctly-scoped and will be exercised perfectly once its already-planned UI PR lands in days' from 'this feature is actually broken/abandoned.' Both collapse to the same undifferentiated CND today.
breaks.fix: Add a sub-verdict tag distinguishing CND(no-front-door-yet) from CND(execution-failed) / CND(hostile-class-failed). When the harness detects the gap is purely a missing rendering surface (API field present, zero DOM consumers), it should record that explicitly and offer to auto-rerun against a later commit on the same epic/branch lineage once one exists, rather than requiring a fresh manual re-submission that looks identical to a first-time failure.

breaks.detail: The write-set-bound oracle (1.1) is specified for diffing 'the whole store,' which implicitly assumes a relational model where a row's absence of a value is unambiguous. EAP/Snuba here is a sparse wide-attribute store where this diff's own code chooses to OMIT the assertion_failure_data key entirely on a passing check rather than writing an explicit null. The theory doesn't yet say whether the oracle should treat 'key absent in new row' as a confirmed non-effect or as an unverified gap — and if a harness's diff logic treats 'absent' the same as 'confirmed null,' it would silently pass over exactly the stale-data-leakage bug class the negative claim is designed to catch.
breaks.fix: Extend mechanism 1.1 with an explicit rule for sparse/wide-column stores: a negative claim ('no failure data on a passing check') is only confirmed if the harness reads back that check's specific row and observes either an explicit null OR a confirmed key-miss at the storage layer, distinguished from a query-time default/fallback value — not merely 'the API response didn't include the field.'

breaks.detail: CONJURE's 'compose from repo topology' worked here only because I happened to check devservices/config.yml; nothing in the theory's mechanisms requires the harness to verify that a declared remote devservice (uptime-checker) is pinned to a SHA that actually implements the feature under test, versus an older/newer main-branch snapshot that predates or has diverged from the assertion-evaluation logic this PR assumes exists on the wire. A silently stale or ahead cross-repo dependency could produce a false ACQUIT (checker never fails, so no failure data ever appears — read as 'feature not reachable, N/A') or a false CND for the wrong reason.
breaks.fix: When CONJURE composes a devservice from a separate repo, record and report the exact SHA/tag pulled, and require the pre-registered claim to name the minimum cross-repo capability it depends on (here: 'uptime-checker must support assertion evaluation and emit assertion_failure_data') so a harness can fail fast with 'dependency capability missing' rather than silently degrading to CND.

newVectors: FW-15 'UI-pending backend slice': a correctly-scoped, backend-only PR in a deliberately incremental (FE/BE-split) delivery process has no possible WORKS verdict under the theory as written, because the exact-code-fingerprint binding and front-door-only constraint jointly eliminate any observable surface — distinct from FW-12 (fixture-vs-prod divergence) and FW-14 (config/flag drift) because the gap here is purely temporal/sequencing, not environmental.

Sparse-attribute-store ambiguity: 'diff the whole store' (1.1) is under-specified for wide-column/EAP-style stores where omitting a key and writing an explicit null are different on-disk states but may be indistinguishable through the read API — a new sub-case of oracle mislocation specific to this class of storage engine, worth naming separately from FW-1 since relational-store assumptions don't transfer.
openQuestions: Does EAP/Snuba's attribute read path ever fall back to a default/adjacent value when a queried attribute key is absent on a given row, or does it reliably return null/missing — this determines whether the sparse-omission pattern in eap_converter.py is actually exploitable or just stylistically inconsistent.

When PR #107065's frontend tree UI landed 5 days later, did it get its own independent test coverage that exercises a real (not fixture-constructed) assertion_failure_data payload end-to-end from a live checker run, or does the whole epic's test suite universally construct assertion_failure_data via the same hand-authored fixtures I saw in this diff (create_uptime_result / create_eap_uptime_result), meaning FW-12 (fixture-world divergence) applies to the entire epic, not just this slice?

Is there an internal Sentry test environment where the real uptime-checker (Rust service) is actually run against assertions in CI today, or does Sentry's own test suite for this feature also stub the checker's output, i.e. does even Sentry's own CI observe genuine cross-repo behavior for this feature?
sonnetDifficulty: The theory application itself, once I had the right diff in hand, was not the hard part. What actually consumed nearly all my effort was PR SELECTION: I sampled roughly 15 candidate 'large feature' PRs across three different feature areas (uptime assertions, user-feedback AI titles, feature-flag suspect heuristics) before discovering, empirically and by brute-force file-list inspection, that getsentry/sentry systematically ships frontend and backend changes in separate PRs — there is no repo doc that states this convention up front, and a more capable model might have inferred the pattern after 2-3 samples instead of ~10. I also had to manually reconstruct a 5-PR timeline via mergedAt timestamps to determine what code existed 'at review time' for the diff under test, and at one point nearly mis-concluded that two sibling PRs (#106833 and #106895) were duplicate/conflicting diffs before realizing this was just how GitHub's per-PR .diff endpoint reports overlapping base-to-head deltas — a bookkeeping error that, if it had gone uncaught, could have corrupted my CND-vs-WORKS boundary (e.g. by wrongly crediting an earlier commit with UI that didn't exist yet, manufacturing a false WORKS). That kind of silent multi-PR timeline reconstruction is exactly the place a Sonnet-level driver can get it wrong without noticing, which is a genuine genius-dependence signal for this theory's practical execution.
